_note: Real ML Kit line output for a THREE-COLUMN business card, captured 2026-09-03. The name sits in the left column, the title in the middle, the logo lockup on the right, and all three share one row.
_anonymised: Boxes are exactly as ML Kit reported them, converted from the captured centre-y and height. The person's name, the company name, the email, the telephone numbers and the street address are replaced by strings of the same shape - same word counts, character classes, lengths and OCR damage, including the accented 'i' the recogniser produced in the road name. Generic job titles and industry words are left as printed: they identify nobody on their own and the classifier rules turn on their real wording.
_source: Samsung SM-G736B, ML Kit text-recognition, Latin. Line angles between -2.0 and +0.9 degrees - a squarely framed card, so the row sharing is layout and not skew.
_layout: Left column: name, then the email. Middle column: title, then the association role. Right column: the logo lockup and its tagline. Full-width lines beneath: company, address, telephones, website.
_why_it_matters: The name and the middle column's title sit 1.545 line heights apart on the same row and must stay two lines. A different card (card_label_beside_number.json) has a caption 1.5625 heights from its own number that must merge. The must-split gap is the tighter of the two, so no single MAX_GAP satisfies both.
